elements.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
elements.evidence: Article XXII as rendered reads "NO RIGHT OF FIRST REFUSAL The Licensor shall have no right of first refusal, right to match or similar right with respect to any offer received by the Licensee from a third party." The disclosure/first-refusal window in original p0139 (notice of a bonafide third-party offer plus a five-business-day Exercise Period before Licensee may proceed) is deleted, and the conditional trigger in p0140 is removed so that "The Licensee shall have the right to consummate the transaction with the third party" is unconditional. No other cited provision imposes a best-terms or match obligation on the Licensee (pricing at p0056-p0067 and p0078 is tier-based with no best-terms undertaking).

elements.element: The Customer MFN covers only a defined product.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: after the edit there is no Customer-side MFN, right-to-match or most-favoured-offer mechanic left in Article XXII, so the scope condition has nothing to attach to.

elements.element: The Customer MFN lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: the "During the term of this Agreement" duration language of p0139 is deleted along with the Right of First Refusal itself, so no Customer MFN period runs at all (the 36-month/seven-year term at p0049 no longer carries any match obligation).

elements.element: The Customer MFN contains reasonable like-for-like comparison carve-outs.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: with the match mechanic removed there is no comparison exercise requiring like-for-like carve-outs.

The defined terms "Right of First Refusal" and "Exercise Period" were created and used only inside Article XXII; both the definitions and their only operative use (the p0140 condition) are removed together, leaving no dangling cross-reference. The Change of Control consent mechanic at p0134 is untouched and does not depend on Article XXII.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the operative text now expressly negates any Licensor right of first refusal, right to match or similar right, which is the playbook's target mechanic (a disclosure/right-to-match/most-favoured-offer obligation burdening Customer is treated as MFN).

Fallback elements are vacuously met because the underlying Customer-side mechanic no longer exists; the finding correctly targets the preferred level rather than negotiating a scoped 12-month match right.

Minimality holds: only Article XXII is touched. The conforming edit to the follow-on sentence is necessary, not cosmetic, because the retained condition ("In the event the Licensor declines or fails to exercise in full the Right of First Refusal before the expiration of the Exercise Period") would otherwise reference deleted defined terms and leave Licensee's right to consummate hanging on a trigger that can never occur. No survival tail, expense language, procedure or extra requirement was added.

The substituted negative sentence is a concise replacement rather than an added obligation; it imposes nothing new on either party and is an acceptable insertion in place of striking the article outright. Note for the drafter: a bare deletion of Article XXII would have been equally sufficient, so the express negation is at the outer edge of minimality but does not fail it.

Intent is preserved: pricing tiers (p0056-p0067), Supplemental Payments (p0078), the term/extension mechanic (p0049) and the separate Change of Control consent right (p0134) all survive without contradiction, and Licensee retains the affirmative right to consummate a third-party transaction.

Drafting check to confirm on the full document: verify no provision outside Article XXII cross-references "Right of First Refusal" or "Exercise Period"; if one does, it must be conformed in the same redline.
